scope: Product Admin native-first GraphQL fallback mutation public and private diagnostic boundaries

findings.finding: All eleven native-first fallback commands already mapped final GraphqlHttpError variants into the Product Admin static public envelope while retaining typed variant classification and stable codes.

GraphqlFallbackMutationContext::map_error still emitted raw_error = ?error in both severity branches. Http and Graphql variants could therefore copy complete backend-controlled status or server-message payloads into structured tracing.

The smallest compatible fix preserves typed matching, public errors, codes, correlation, severity and request-shape diagnostics while retaining only payload presence and character length for Http and Graphql. Network and Unauthorized retain no invented payload.

Each wrapper still invokes exactly one unchanged compatibility executor. The executor performs one native server call and invokes one existing GraphQL mutation only after native failure; no retry or second fallback is introduced.

Catalog-options, primary/category reads and primary mutations retain their bounded diagnostic policies and focused guards. This slice changes only the separate fallback mutation mapper and its evidence surface.

The known Product Admin catalog-options, read, primary mutation and fallback mutation GraphQL diagnostic envelopes no longer intentionally retain complete backend error payloads. Browser, mounted execution and broader ecommerce owners remain open.
